subject.title: Feature: pairing list-approved and pairing revoke commands

question: Should OpenClaw add a terminal pairing-management surface now, and if so should it be narrow `pairing list-approved`/`pairing revoke` commands or part of the broader contact/permission inventory tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48620?
rationale: The requested commands expose and mutate authorization state and overlap existing `/allowlist`, channel status, and broader contact inventory surfaces, so the permanent product/security boundary needs maintainer direction.

options.title: Fold into contact inventory
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48620 as the canonical design for one account-scoped inventory and management surface, including approved pairings and revocation.

options.title: Ship narrow pairing CLI
options.body: Add only approved-pairing list and revoke commands with explicit account scoping, redaction, and tests, leaving broader contact rows for later.

options.title: Keep chat-only management
options.body: Continue relying on in-chat `/allowlist` and manual config/store management until maintainers choose a broader admin UX.

recommendation.title: Fold into contact inventory
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48620 as the canonical design for one account-scoped inventory and management surface, including approved pairings and revocation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest shared history signal across `/allowlist`, pairing CLI, and channel status boundaries relevant to this product decision.
